posts.text:
US pension funds are heavily concentrated in technology stocks:

The technology sector accounts for 44% of total US pension fund equity allocation, according to a Bloomberg analysis of more than 70 pension funds.

This percentage has more than doubled since 2015.

Pension fund equity allocation to technology is now larger than that of the next 3 sectors combined.

By comparison, Financials represent 16%, followed by Healthcare at 12%, Industrials at 11%, and Consumer stocks at 10%.

To put this into perspective, the Consumer sector was these funds' largest allocation in 2014, at ~20%.

US pension funds are more exposed to technology stocks than ever.

President Trump’s been tested like almost no other leader in American history.
He watched an election he believes was stolen in 2020, then faced 37 separate legal cases designed to keep him off the ballot and bankrupt him. He’s survived two assassination attempts, where bullets came within inches of ending his life. Through it all, the raids, the trials, the media attacks, the isolation, he never broke. He never quit.
He came back in 2024 and won in a landslide so big they couldn’t rig it. And here’s what a lot of people don’t know, he doesn’t take a salary as president. He’s put his entire business empire on hold, stepped away from a billionaire lifestyle, and chosen to serve instead.

That’s why so many Americans look at him and see a fighter who puts America First, no matter the cost. The man just keeps standing, and he keeps fighting for this country.

Palantir CEO Alex Karp is signaling a shift toward Democrats following their midterm victories, criticizing Trump's immigration crackdown and Republicans' approach to economic justice. 

Despite securing billions in federal contracts under Trump, Karp said Democrats had corrected course enough to potentially win his support in 2028.

“I've been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far left environment. I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet,” Karp said.

On immigration, Karp welcomed Trump's acknowledgment that enforcement had gone too far, saying: “I'm glad he's saying in public now what I've been saying in private.”

Source: POLITICO

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over why Megaspeed, an Nvidia $NVDA customer accused of funneling US chips to China, isn’t on the government’s trade blacklist, per Axios.

“How come Megaspeed isn’t on the entities list?” Bessent asked during a meeting in the White House Situation Room last Thursday, according to sources familiar with it.

“I don’t know. I’ll look into it,” Lutnick replied, per Axios. Sources say Lutnick had resisted acting despite intelligence warnings, for fear of escalating the trade war with China.

The Commerce Department’s Entity List blocks companies seen as national security risks from getting sensitive US technology.
